_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees` and
say why in `note`.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The note is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges. A SHA
written during a PR names the branch commit, which stops existing the
moment the PR lands — so the gate that was green locally went red on main
and needed a follow-up commit that changed nothing but a SHA. That cost six
fixes in the two days the SHA-based version existed. Squashing rewrites
history, not content, so an object id simply survives it, along with
rebases, cherry-picks and force pushes.

docs/IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md.note: Two commits reviewed. 4e3b223 changes which exception MailConnectionProbe throws when the server rejects a login: MailAuthenticationException instead of MailConnectionException, so the reply text stops being rendered into the user-facing error.mail.connectionFailed placeholder and travels as the cause into the log instead. That narrows what server-controlled text reaches the UI; it touches no TLS, auth-mechanism or timeout setting. Re-checked on the probe specifically: pinned ssl.checkserveridentity, the fail-closed OAuth2-requires-SSL guard and the millisecond-string timeouts are all unchanged. 5c76f91 adds an outbound content type: MimeMessageBuilder attaches a text/html alternative rendered by the new MarkdownBodyRenderer when the composed body uses Markdown. The HTML is generated locally from the user's own keystrokes, never from server-controlled data, so the hostile-server surface this boundary is about is untouched — as are TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path. Re-checked the send path specifically: the CRLF guard on header-bound fields (requireSingleLine) and both AddressPolicy branches are unchanged, and drafts stay single-part text/plain, so the IMAP APPEND payload shape is identical to what was audited. The renderer runs with escapeHtml and sanitizeUrls on and HtmlBlock parsing off, so it cannot emit script, event handlers or non-http/mailto URLs; rendering is skipped above 512 kB, below the existing 10 MB body cap, so it adds no unbounded CPU sink to the send path. Verdict stays PASS. Third commit reviewed: the conversation-scope change adds FolderRole.SENT to CONVERSATION_EXCLUDED_ROLES in MailFacade, which under this path is two functional lines (the role list and a log string) plus javadoc. It moves nothing this boundary is about: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently — the change decides which folders a read-path query counts. Two effects re-checked because they do reach IMAP. (1) The listing now resolves a fourth folder role per page, through the same bounded findFolderNamesByRoleWithoutWaiting call the other three already used, with the same fail-closed handling: an unresolvable role still degrades the whole listing to folder-scoped rather than guessing an exclusion set. (2) The resolved names are attacker-controlled (the server names its folders) and now include the sent folder, but they ride the same :excludedFolders JPQL parameter binding as before, so the NOT IN clause gains a value, not a new injection surface; the list stays bounded by the folders the server reports for those roles, which was already true of trash, junk and drafts. Verdict stays PASS. Fourth commit reviewed: the setext-heading fix in MarkdownBodyRenderer. It renders strictly less, not more — a paragraph followed by a --- or === rule used to become a heading and is now demoted back to a paragraph, so bodies that only tripped that rule no longer produce an HTML alternative at all. Input is unchanged in kind: the composed body, the user's own keystrokes, never server-controlled bytes, so the hostile-server surface this boundary is about is untouched, as are TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path. Re-checked the three things that could have moved. (1) The re-appended underline is taken from the source body and inserted as a Text node, so it goes through the same escapeHtml pass as any other text — it cannot introduce markup, and sanitizeUrls and the HtmlBlock-off setting are unchanged. (2) includeSourceSpans(BLOCKS) was added to the parser purely to tell ATX from setext; comparing parse trees with and without it confirmed it does not change parsing, only annotates blocks. (3) No new unbounded work in the send path: the tree walk is linear in nodes, and the one added allocation (splitting the body into lines) happens only when a setext heading was actually found, still under the existing 512 kB render cap. Drafts remain single-part text/plain, so the IMAP APPEND payload shape is still what was audited. Verdict stays PASS. Same review extended to the follow-up in that commit: ENABLED_BLOCKS moved from Set.of to an explicitly ordered LinkedHashSet. This removes nondeterminism rather than adding behaviour — CommonMark registers block parsers in iteration order and Set.of salts that order per JVM, so the renderer produced different documents for the same body between runs (six runs of one parse: five headings, one thematic break). The set contains the same five block types as before, so no parser is added or removed and no new construct becomes renderable; only the tie-break between heading and thematic break for a rule under a paragraph is now fixed instead of random. Nothing here reaches TLS, auth, timeouts or any IMAP command path, and the inbound parsing this boundary is about uses MimePartExtractor, not this renderer. Verdict stays PASS. Fifth commit reviewed: the thread-position fix, whose whole diff under this path is one file, ThreadingService.java. attachToExistingThread stops assigning max(threadPosition) + 1 and instead appends only when a COUNT reports that nothing in the thread sorts after the arrival, renumbering the thread otherwise through the same pass reconcileLateArrivingParent already used. Nothing this boundary is about moves: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently — In-Reply-To, References and the subject normalization feed the same lookups as before, and the References walk keeps its MAX_REFERENCES_WALK cap. The one thing that could have moved a verdict is resource use on the sync path, which is what B1-1 and B1-2 were both about, so it was weighed rather than waved through. The renumbering pass loads a thread's members as managed entities, @Lob bodies included, so a hostile server drip-feeding a large thread in descending date order could make each arrival re-read the whole thread: quadratic in thread length, with the bodies in the heap. That exposure is not new and its worst case is unchanged — the same pass already ran on every orphan merge, and on an initial sync those dominate, because MessageDownloader walks UIDs newest-first, so a reply is threaded before its parent and reaches the merge branch rather than this one. The new branch fires only for an arrival that is both older than an existing member and already has a mirrored parent, which that same newest-first walk makes the exception rather than the rule. The COUNT that decides it is bounded and served by the existing (account_id, thread_id) index. Recorded as a known cost rather than closed: teaching the renumber to read a body-free projection would remove the heap term from both call sites and is worth its own change. Verdict stays PASS.

docs/UPDATER_AUDIT.md.note: c16b3df adds the tray icon, its menu and close-to-tray under frontend/src-tauri/src. The updater itself is untouched: endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are unchanged, as are tauri.conf.json (CSP, updater plugin config) and capabilities/default.json — the new commands are app-defined and therefore not capability-gated, and the tray is built Rust-side. New surface reviewed: three commands (configure_tray, set_tray_tooltip, set_close_behavior) that take only strings and a bool from the webview and reach nothing but tray label/tooltip APIs and an in-process Mutex<bool>; a CloseRequested handler that hides the main window; and a tray menu whose Quit calls the same app.exit(0) the window path already reaches. None of that touches signature verification or the download path, so the B6 verdict does not move. Flagged for the next full B6 pass rather than settled here: tauri-plugin-single-instance is a new supply-chain item (32 crates added to Cargo.lock) and opens a local IPC channel (a named object on Windows) that another process on the same machine can address — low risk under the single-user local threat model, but it is new attack surface under an audited path, not a reshuffle of existing code. cargo audit is clean after the change apart from the pre-existing allowed RUSTSEC-2026-0190 in anyhow. Re-reviewed for the follow-up fixes in the same paths: the CloseBehavior default flips to quitting, set_close_behavior refuses to enable hiding without a tray icon, and a failed tray build is logged rather than propagated out of setup. All three narrow what the shell does on a failure path and none of them touch the updater, the capability set or the CSP, so the verdict is unmoved. df1323a touches this path in one file, UpdatePromptDialog.svelte, and only below its script block: the inline Dialog.Root/Portal/Overlay/Content scaffolding becomes the shared DialogShell plus DialogTitle/DialogDescription, and the hand-written aria-describedby goes because bits-ui already derives it from the description. The visible effect is the corner radius, rounded-lg to rounded-2xl. Nothing the B6 trust chain rests on is in this file, and the entries that do hold it are byte-identical for this commit — verified as an empty diff for src-tauri/src, tauri.conf.json, capabilities, updates.ts and AboutSettings.svelte, so the endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are untouched. Re-checked the two things in this dialog that could have moved. (1) The install path is unchanged: both buttons still call postponePromptedUpdate and installPromptedUpdate and both still carry disabled={installing}, so an install in flight still cannot be re-triggered or postponed from here. (2) Dismissal is unchanged: handleOpenChange still refuses to postpone while installing, and DialogShell passes open and onOpenChange straight to Dialog.Root, so escape and outside-click behave exactly as before. Verdict stays PASS. The design-system sweep touches this path in one file, AboutSettings.svelte, and the whole commit diff for it is a single line: the status dot's dotClass moves from the raw Tailwind bg-emerald-500 to the new bg-success token. That dot belongs to notificationStatus, the SSE connection indicator, and not to the update check — the update surface in this file is byte-identical (the checkForUpdateManually import, handleCheckForUpdates, updateCheckStatus and the channel selector), as are the other twelve Code paths entries, so the endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are untouched, and so is the manual-check failure UI with its RELEASES_URL fallback that §5 rests on. The colour was measured rather than picked: --success is 3.38:1 against the page, which is what a non-text indicator owes, and unlike the emerald it replaces it takes its dark-mode value from the token layer instead of a hand-written dark: class. Nothing here reaches signature verification or the download path. Verdict stays PASS. 3802b45 touches this path in one file, AboutSettings.svelte, and the whole diff for it is the update-channel Field: its <Select> moves inside an explicit children snippet and the hand-written aria-describedby="update-channel-select-hint" becomes {...control}, spread from the props Field now derives. Unlike the previous entry the channel selector itself is therefore not byte-identical, so the two things it could have moved were checked. (1) The rendered markup is the same: the Field carries a hint and no error, and fieldControlProps then emits exactly aria-describedby="update-channel-select-hint" plus an undefined aria-invalid, which Svelte omits — that derivation is the hint-only case covered by ui/field/field.test.ts. (2) The behaviour is untouched: value={$updateChannel}, onchange={handleUpdateChannelChange} and the UPDATE_CHANNELS option set are unchanged, so the stored channel preference that check_for_update(channel) routes on cannot have moved. Everything else the B6 trust chain rests on is byte-identical for this commit — the checkForUpdateManually import, handleCheckForUpdates, updateCheckStatus and the manual-check failure UI with its RELEASES_URL fallback that §5 rests on, as are the other twelve Code paths entries, so the endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are untouched. Nothing here reaches signature verification or the download path. Verdict stays PASS.

docs/API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md.note: 3c2e1b3 touches this path in documentation only: ConversationSummaryResponse gains a reworded record javadoc and a reworded @Schema description for messageCount, because the conversation scope stopped spanning the sent folder. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no validation annotation was touched — so none of the things this audit weighs (request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes) moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for the commit is a single description string, and the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by exactly the one @description comment line that carries it — no type, field name or optionality in the generated client surface moves. Verdict stays PASS. — 9567d49 moves the address book out of the account scope: the contact endpoints go from /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts and .../contact-labels to /api/v1/contacts and /api/v1/contact-labels, and both controllers lose their accountId path variable (autocomplete keeps it as a @RequestParam @Positive). Nothing this audit weighs moves with them. Authorization is path-independent: SecurityConfig permits only PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (the OAuth callbacks) and leaves anyRequest().authenticated() behind ApiKeyFilter, so a relocated path keeps the same posture — there is no per-prefix rule to fall out of. The two counts the enumeration rests on are unchanged (17 @RestController, 12 @Validated): no controller was added, removed, or stripped of @Validated. Every bound §2 cites is untouched — bulk 100 items, merge 9 sources / 10 emails, label assignment 100 contacts / 50 labels, label name 60 chars, contactQueryMaxLength and the contactAutocompleteMaxLimit clamp — and the whole contact/dto diff for this commit is a single javadoc line; account/dto only gains @Nullable on MailProviderResponse.oauth2RegistrationId, which springdoc does not read, so the golden api-docs.json does not move for it. Error hygiene is unchanged in shape: the contact exceptions drop their accountId argument and still resolve through AppException to an RFC 9457 ProblemDetail. The audit enumerates no endpoint paths, so the move leaves no stale claim. Verdict stays PASS. — 472de85 touches this path in documentation only: the ThreadResponse record javadoc drops the hedge that threadPosition order matches receivedAt ascending only for the canonical case, because ThreadingService now places every arrival by its own receivedAt instead of appending it. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no @Schema description or validation annotation was touched, so none of the things this audit weighs — request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes — moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json does not appear in the commit diff at all and OpenApiSnapshotTest passes, so the generated client surface cannot have moved either; springdoc reads @Schema, not record javadoc. What changed is the truth of a claim the endpoint already made about its own ordering, not the shape of what it returns. Verdict stays PASS.

docs/CONTENT_RENDERING_AUDIT.md.note: bc0363d touches this path in exactly one file — MessageMoveControl.svelte, the folder picker in the detail toolbar; the whole directory diff for the commit is that file, and the other six Code paths entries are unchanged (verified: an empty diff for content-sanitizer.ts, mailFrame.ts, HtmlSanitizer.java and MimePartExtractor.java). The change is de-duplication, not behaviour: an inline {#each} over $folders becomes the shared MoveTargetMenuItems.svelte, and an inline filter becomes moveTargetsFor(). Nothing on the untrusted-body path moves — MessageContent.svelte, which hosts the opaque-origin sandbox iframe, and messageHeadingContext.ts are byte-identical. The only server-controlled string this file renders is a folder display name, which an IMAP server chooses, and it reaches the DOM exactly as before: Svelte text interpolation in a span plus a title attribute, auto-escaped, in the old inline markup and in the extracted component alike. Neither carries {@html} (grepped across the directory and the new component), and no email body, header or attachment value is read here at all. The three layers the verdict rests on — backend Jsoup safelist, frontend DOM allow-list, sandboxed iframe with the hash-pinned meta CSP — are untouched, as is the remote-image opt-in. Verdict stays PASS. df1323a touches the same one file again, and the whole directory diff for the commit is two lines of it: an import, and the folder menu's literal class string replaced by menuContentVariants({ scroll: true }) from the new shared ui/menu. The rendered classes are the same set in a different order (z-10, rounded-lg, border, bg-popover, p-1, text-popover-foreground, shadow-lg, min-w-44, max-h-64, overflow-y-auto), confirmed against the running app. This is styling only: no markup, no attribute and no data flow in the file changes, the folder display name — still the one server-controlled string here — reaches the DOM through the same auto-escaped text interpolation, and there is no {@html} anywhere in the directory or in the shared module (grepped). MessageContent.svelte with the opaque-origin sandbox iframe and messageHeadingContext.ts are byte-identical, and so are the other six Code paths entries. Verdict stays PASS.

docs/OAUTH_AUDIT.md.note: The commit this id records is the change the audit's own v1.2 revision describes, so the doc and the code were written against each other rather than the doc trailing the code. Recorded here rather than by bumping `Audited commit` because the SHA would name a pre-squash branch commit that stops existing on merge — the failure mode this ledger was built for. Diff read in full: the login flow gains a fourth fail-fast guard in OAuth2LoginService (granted scopes vs. the provider's required mail scopes, rejecting before persistence), OAuth2ClaimsExtractor gains requiredMailScopes(), and the Google and Microsoft extractors state theirs. The other four Code paths entries are untouched — verified as an empty diff for SecurityConfig.java, OAuth2CompletedStateTracker.java, ExternalProviderLoginService.java and resources/static, so PKCE, the state gate and the failure-redirect hygiene are byte-identical. Checked the three things that could have moved a verdict. (1) The check only ever rejects: it compares two sets and throws, it never adds a scope to a request, so the E-row claim that scopes are hardcoded in application.properties with no in-app escalation path still holds exactly. (2) It cannot resurrect a dead account — it runs before persistence and calls markRequiresReauthIfExists, the same direction as the refresh-token guard, so the flag is still cleared only by a login that is complete. (3) No token material reaches a log: the WARN line names the missing scope constants and a masked email, and the audit entry carries the same, so the log-hygiene claim in §2 is unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.
